text:
Mike L: seeing a bunch of gRPC stream stalls from pod->pod calls hitting GPU nodes during large batched uploads. started ~07:10 UTC, affects model ingest paths :sob:
Anya P: which errors do you see? stream resets or timeouts?
Mike L: stream resets. logs show 'gRPC: stream failed: io: read/write on closed pipe' and kernel dmesg on node shows 'fragmented datagram, size 9050, EINVAL' around same time
Deepak R: that screams MTU + encap. we recently enabled geneve on the subnet for cross-az overlay right?
Mike L: yeah we pushed geneve overlay last week and bumped host MTU to 9000 but the ENI in some AZs is 1500 so likely mismatch
sre-oncall: quick checks: can you run ping -M do -s 8500 <peer> from affected pod and from host, and ip link show for vxlan/geneve and host interfaces?
Mike L: ran from host: ping -M do -s 8500 -> frag needed. from pod (inside netns): ping works but traces show large fragments, throughput drops when jobs push >1MB messages
Anya P: also check GSO/GRO offload — encap+gso combos can create oversized skbs that get dropped by hardware or ECMP path device
Deepak R: exact commands I ran on a repro node: ``ip link show dev geneve0 && ethtool -k eth0 | grep gso && cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_mtu_probing``
Deepak R: tcp_mtu_probing was 0. geneve0 mtu is 9000, eth0 mtu 1500 on a subset of nodes (weird).
Mike L: interestingly only GPU nodes where RDMA is enabled show the stalls consistently
Anya P: RDMA NICs sometimes bypass kernel PMTU handling for performance; if their PFs are clamped at 1500 the encap packets from geneve0 will be too big and get chopped -> gRPC streaming will see backpressure and resets
sre-oncall: mitigation ideas: 1) set net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 clusterwide (helpful for transient PMTU discovery), 2) set overlay mtu to 1450 to account for encap overhead, 3) disable GSO on the tunnel/host for affected nodes as a stop-gap
Mike L: can we do a rolling config: set tunnel mtu to 1450 in CNI config and restart kube-proxy on a few nodes?
Deepak R: yes CNI change is safest long-term. For quick rollback we patched sysctl via node-init to enable tcp_mtu_probing and disabled gso on eth0: ``ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off``
Anya P: note disabling GSO/TSO increases CPU on networking path — fine as temporary for low-traffic AZs but not for sustained throughput on large clusters
Mike L: ran an A/B on two GPU nodes: node A (gso off + mtp_probe=1) stable, node B (unchanged) stalled within 2 mins under load.
sre-oncall: created an alert rule to detect repeated 'gRPC: stream reset' + pkts dropped >100/s on node. if it fires we autoschedule some traffic away from nodes with mismatched mtu
Mike L: file with logs and repro steps uploaded to /mnt/logs/pod-stream-stall-2061234567.txt and to the incident board.
Deepak R: long term: make sure all NIC/ENI MTUs align with overlay config during provisioning. add a preflight check in node bootstrap that validates eth mtu >= overlay mtu + encap_overhead. If mismatch fail bootstrap or auto-correct MTU.
Anya P: +1. Also add a note to RDMA onboarding docs: verify that SR-IOV or RDMA drivers support offload for tunnels or force host MTU to a safe value.
sre-oncall: I will open a PR to the cluster-provisioner to validate MTU and to the CNI defaults to use conservative 1450 for host-geneveVXLAN encapsulation. tagging @infra-team for rollout plan :thumbsup:
Mike L: thanks. for now we have a hotfix patch rolling to GPU nodes in affected AZs. will monitor. :eyes:
k8s-bot: deploy-bot: rollout gpu-node-mtu-hotfix to az-west-2 started (23 nodes)
Mike L: closing thread once rollout completes. if anyone sees residual stalls ping me or @sre-oncall
